speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Therefore, like regular employees, casual work employees are entitled to timely payment of salary, CPF and protection against wrongful dismissal.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: They are also entitled to paid annual and sick leave if they have been employed for at least three months.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Other jurisdictions might have seen an increase in the number of self-employed persons (SEPs) engaging in casual work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In Singapore, we cannot equate SEPs with casual workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For example, taxi drivers are self-employed but work regular shifts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Nonetheless, the proportion of SEPs who did self-employed work as their main job has remained stable at 8% to 10% of our resident workforce over the past decade.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In fact, there was a drop in the number of SEPs last year, due in part to the tighter job market.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Our surveys show that many SEPs choose to be self-employed for greater flexibility and autonomy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In 2017, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) convened a Tripartite Workgroup on SEPs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The workgroup consulted extensively with SEPs and other stakeholders, such as SEP associations and service-buyers, and considered practices in other jurisdictions as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: First, the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) launched its voluntary mediation services last year to assist SEPs in resolving disputes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The tripartite partners are also encouraging adoption of the Tripartite Standard on Contracting with SEPs and the key terms of engagement form template to minimise disputes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Second, we made available prolonged medical leave insurance products for SEPs to enhance their protection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Third, we are working with the tripartite partners and SEP associations to ensure that SEPs have access to both technical and non-technical skills training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Government, as a service-buyer, will take the lead to pilot this savings model next year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For those seeking alternatives to casual work or self-employment, there is a wide range of support under the Government’s Adapt and Grow initiative.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: They can approach career centres run by Workforce Singapore and NTUC's Employment and Employability Institute for assistance.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I understand that a labour task force actually found that there is a third category of workers called the dependent workers.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: This would be workers who the Ministry cannot correctly categorise as either employees or self-employed persons.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Examples of such dependent workers are typically the ones who actually choose to sell their services only to one company, the likes of Grab drivers and Deliveroo deliveryman.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: How are we supporting this group of dependent workers?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, to a certain sense, one of the major issues that we have seen in countries, such as the United Kingdom and Italy, where they have created a separate category, is that you find employees being classified there or you find misclassification to try to game the system by providing them less benefits.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To some extent, there are two problems that we found.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: One, we found that in misclassification, employees received weaker protection; at the same time, businesses also got smarter, they then change the contracting models to fully or partially avoid obligations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, in Singapore, for example, if you are classified as SEP, employers do not pay for CPF, for example, so you will have to fork out yourself.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, in a certain sense, the terms are very different and they are not covered against term.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, I think we will keep to the current model.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But where we will do more are schemes in which, for example, for low-wage workers, we have got Workfare to support them and other forms of employability-type schemes, such as training and insurance, so that we can support them better.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I have personally come across casual workers who are sometimes wrongly classified as own account workers, self-employed, freelance, independent contractors, contract-for-service.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: So, can we do more and can MOM have a more robust approach to errant employers as well as a better outreach to such casual workers?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In fact, that was what I was mentioning just now.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If we create new segments of workers, then all the more you will find employers or some industries trying to game the system.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Each case that MOM and CPF Board investigate could involve more than one worker.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Those are the protection they get as employees.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Penalties, including warning and late payment interest charges, were meted out to the companies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Two companies which refused to make the necessary payments to the affected employees were prosecuted.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: One subsequently fully settled the arrears out of Court while the other is currently appealing against this conviction.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, rest assured that MOM and CPF Board will investigate the cases.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If misclassification is established, we will ensure that employers make good their obligations and to pay back the affected employees what they were due, including overtime pay and CPF contributions.
